title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I have been upon the point of writing to thee for many days, and now so good an opportunity presents that no longer I put off. But inform thee, my dear Mother, that our family is in good health, in which state we found them on the seventh day evening after leaving Baltimore. We left the city on first day, stayed at New Market until third day & then traveled home in company with William Wood. Caleb is still here, what will be his employment this winter is not yet determined. William Troth has commenced school at Redstone. Mary’s sister Miriam has likewise got a little school in Bridgeport. We have got a little boy that the overseers of the poor will bind to us if we think proper to keep him.

Our corn is tolerable good which we are now gathering, indeed our country smiles with plenty, compared with the prospect toward Baltimore. But money Mother, I cannot get, therefore must remain poor & in debt. I have understood that Henry Smith
has requested a certificate for himself & wife to Baltimore monthly meeting which if obtained I understand they intend moving this season right off, & I think from home completely.

Uncle Jonas & Aunt Elizabeth are as well as usual. Uncle said if he had known that he should have had his health so well & so many of his dear Friends at Baltimore, that he should have tried to have performed the journey.

I should love to live amongst my relations & dear Friends, let that be where it might. My love for those where sentiments & manners I believe to be right, does more & more increase, notwithstanding I always loved such.

postscript.p: Mary’s love is affectionately addressed to the above mentioned
